meta_description: Learn how tolerance defaults and standard finishing line items affect your CNC quotes. Understand 2D vs 3D tolerances, deburring, and Ra 125 surface roughness.

sections.heading: Comparing CNC Quotes? Here’s What Tolerance and Finishing Line Items Actually Mean
sections.text: Comparing CNC Quotes? Here’s What Tolerance and Finishing Line Items Actually Mean by James Wright | Aug 5, 2026 « Back to all posts Two quotes for the same part can differ by a real margin and both be “correct” — because they’re not always quoting the same thing. Tolerance defaults vary by process, and a “standard finish” isn’t a fixed baseline across shops. Knowing what each term actually buys you is the difference between comparing apples to apples and picking the cheaper number without knowing why it’s cheaper. Quick Summary 2D (sheet) parts default to ±0.01″ tolerance; 3D (machined) parts default to ±0.005″ — a real difference tied to the process, not the shop. At eMachineShop, detab a...
